summary: A 26-foot tower with an L-6 cab on Hoover Ridge near Detroit, Oregon, was built in 1932, abandoned in 1948, and is now gone.

facts.design: 26-foot tower with an L-6 cab and a cabin
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1948 and now gone; no source describes what remains at the site.

events.note: Named among eleven new emergency lookout stations for the Santiam district
26-foot tower with L-6 cab and cabin, per the register and firelookout.com
Three new lookout houses planned for the summer, Hoover point among the peaks
Weebly history: a lookout house was constructed, no month given; conflicts with the 1932 build date

notes_for_editor: Build date conflict: the register and firelookout.com give 1932 for the tower and cabin; the Weebly history gives 1936 for a lookout house constructed, and a 1933 plan for Hoover point. The story reports both. Location conflict: the register point (44.742471, -122.099505) is about 1 km from the firelookout.com and FFLA point (44.73536, -122.10728), as the record already notes. No source describes the site today or public access, and no staffing or fire history was found. Two web searches found nothing further on Hoover Ridge or Hoover Point. Whether Hoover point (1933) and Hoover Ridge are the same site is not confirmed by any source.
